_comment: Recent-traffic scenario for neighbor_edges.count decay (#544, PR #574 review F1). Two neighbours of the same node share the hop prefix. A has large old credit and one recent credit; B has a short recent burst. cmd/ingestor/neighbor_edge_decay_test.go credits both edges day by day through the real write path (credits on a day land one hour before that day's decay check; day 0 credits come before the first check, which starts the clock) and asserts the lifetime counts (decay disabled, the default) and the decayed counts (halfLifeDays). cmd/server/neighbor_edge_decay_consumers_test.go feeds both snapshots to the real hop resolver: with lifetime counts the hop resolves to A by affinity, with decayed counts to B. Decay makes affinity follow recent traffic, so an established edge can lose to a newer one.
